source.title: On the Weight Dynamics of Deep Normalized Networks
source.citation: Christian H. X. Ali Mehmeti-Göpel et al., 2023
source.authors: Christian H. X. Ali Mehmeti-Göpel; M. Wand

record.file_problem: none; full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether deep networks with and without residual shortcuts are trainable under different training protocols, using ELR spread and reported accuracy rather than the versions’ training-error measures.
record.gate_note: The study reports training outcomes for NoShort and Short ResNet variants, plus accuracy and ELR spread. It does not report training classification error. Figure-only CIFAR results are recorded as figure-only; cited findings from other studies are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study investigates effective learning-rate dynamics and reports test accuracy and qualitative trainability. It does not measure training classification error or establish depth-dependent training-error degradation under matched training conditions. Its critical learning rate concerns ELR-ratio flipping, not V5's loss-curvature stability threshold. These results therefore do not directly test any supplied version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the empirical conclusion: reducing ELR spread correlates with improved trainability, without proving general causation, and other factors affect performance. The authors identify their theoretical model of normalization-induced weight dynamics as the main contribution; its convergence guarantees assume constant base gradients.
record.recipe_differences: Studies ELR dynamics and interventions in BatchNorm ResNets; it does not reproduce the original studies’ training-error measurements or recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Trainability and ELR spread vary with residual shortcuts, learning-rate schedule, and ELR warm-up or constraint. For real training, super-critical learning rates can prevent ELR convergence; CIFAR-100 results also show a gap between Short and NoShort networks.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-10, warm-up and ELR constraints reduce ELR spread and restore qualitative trainability of ResNet110 NoShort. On CIFAR-100, they yield meaningful but limited performance, with a remaining gap to the shortcut architecture.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reducing layer-wise ELR disparities can improve trainability of deep BatchNorm convolutional networks under the tested SGD recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: On ImageNet after 50 epochs, ResNet101 NoShort test accuracy rises from 8.50% without warm-up to 41.83% with subcritical warm-up and 47.99% with ELR constraints alone. Shortcut models achieve 72.83–73.06%. These are test accuracies, not training-error measurements.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Warm-up and ELR constraints improve test performance of deep networks without shortcuts, while a substantial shortcut advantage remains in this setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Under constant base-gradient assumptions, layer-wise ELR ratios converge at every constant learning rate. In real training, sufficiently high rates can instead produce persistent ELR disparities.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ELR-ratio convergence depends on learning-rate scheduling and on whether normalization-driven dynamics dominate changes in base gradients.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (Proceedings of Machine Learning Research, 2024)
record.problems: The paper says ELR spread and trainability correlation is not proof of a general causal connection. Its CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 accuracy and spread results are shown in figures, and training classification error is not reported.
record.rows_left_out: No rows: the study does not report training classification error, the outcome directly named by the tested claim version. Figure 5, Figure 6, and Table 1 report accuracy and ELR spread instead.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error, including corrupted or random labels.
Spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.

Depth-dependent training-error degradation, its persistence with longer training, its prevention by identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization exceptions. Shortcut comparisons report test accuracy and qualitative trainability instead.
Effects of initialization choices on learning speed and trainable depth; no initialization comparison is performed.
Loss recovery above the initial linearized-model stability limit, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence relative to that threshold.
Training speed and learning-rate tolerance with versus without BatchNorm, and the Fixup exception; all experimental networks use BatchNorm.

record.verdict_notes: The empty row set is appropriate for the supplied versions. The accuracy and ELR results are explicitly declared in rows_left_out, so they are not missing results. Qualitative recovery of trainability does not establish near-zero training error or resolve V3's depth-dependent training-error comparison.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not report training classification error or test random-label/corrupted-label training.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment or neuron-width sweep.

It compares ResNet variants with and without shortcuts and reports trainability, but does not report the training-error measure specified by this version. It does not test depth sweeps, longer training as a control, or plain tanh networks trained with special initialization.
No comparison of initializations or activation-matched initialization methods.
Learning-rate criticality is studied through ELR spread, not the stability threshold, curvature, or squared-loss outcomes specified by this version.
All experimental networks use BatchNorm; there is no with-versus-without BatchNorm comparison, nor a Fixup experiment.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
